Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.45% today to $457.22, continuing a slide that's cost it nearly $21 per share since mid-October. The decline fits a broader pullback in energy stocks as oil prices, while still elevated, have peaked: Brent crude hit $116 earlier this week on Middle East tensions but has since retreated slightly, and the stock has dropped four of the last five trading days as the initial geopolitical panic fades. Refinery utilization remains solid at 93.4%, but with crude inventories rising to 695 million barrels and gasoline stocks elevated, refiners face less pricing power even with oil costs still above $107.

The underlying issue is that while Middle East conflict headlines (Iran-backed Houthis, Saudi interceptions, U.S. tensions with Iran) did spike oil prices in late October, sustained high prices tend to trigger demand destruction—drivers buy less fuel, inventories build—which pressures refiner margins. Marathon's stock rallied on the initial supply shock but has given back those gains as the market appears to be pricing in that geopolitical premiums don't sustain indefinitely without actual supply disruptions.
